\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গর্ভবতী} (gôrbhôbôtī)}{গর্ভবতী (gôrbhôbôtī)}]{\bn{গর্ভবতী} (gôrbhôbôtī) — pregnant}

\label{lesson:BN-C485-gorbhoboti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a generation, then the Bengali for an ancestor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গর্ভবতী}}
\textbf{\bn{গর্ভবতী}} — \emph{gôrbhôbôtī} — \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাকিমা} \bn{গর্ভবতী}, \bn{তাই} \bn{ভারী} \bn{কাজ} \bn{করেন} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kākimā gôrbhôbôtī, tāi bhārī kāj kôren nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My aunt is pregnant, so she doesn't do heavy work.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গর্ভবতী}} (\emph{gôrbhôbôtī}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{garbhavatī}, \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): \emph{garbha}, the womb, with \emph{-vatī}, \textquotedblleft{}having\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôrbhôbôtī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôrbhôbôtī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kākimā gôrbhôbôtī, tāi bhārī kāj kôren nā.} — My aunt is pregnant, so she doesn't do heavy work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a generation, then the Bengali for an ancestor, then say \emph{gôrbhôbôtī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{গর্ভবতী} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Pregnant\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রসব} (prôsôb)}{প্রসব (prôsôb)}]{\bn{প্রসব} (prôsôb) — childbirth; delivery}

\label{lesson:BN-C485-prosob}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an ancestor, then the Bengali for pregnant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রসব}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রসব}} — \emph{prôsôb} — \textquotedblleft{}childbirth; delivery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{হাসপাতালে} \bn{কাকিমার} \bn{প্রসব} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hāspātāle kākimār prôsôb hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My aunt gave birth in hospital.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রসব}} (\emph{prôsôb}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{prasava}, \textquotedblleft{}bringing forth, birth\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôsôb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôsôb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāspātāle kākimār prôsôb hôlô.} — My aunt gave birth in hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an ancestor, then the Bengali for pregnant, then say \emph{prôsôb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জন্মানো} (jônmāno)}{জন্মানো (jônmāno)}]{\bn{জন্মানো} (jônmāno) — to be born}

\label{lesson:BN-C485-jonmano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for pregnant, then the Bengali for childbirth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জন্মানো}}
\textbf{\bn{জন্মানো}} — \emph{jônmāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to be born\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{ভাইঝি} \bn{শীতের} \bn{এক} \bn{সকালে} \bn{জন্মাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmār bhāijhi shīter ek sôkāle jônmālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My niece was born one winter morning.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{শিশু} \bn{হাসপাতালে} \bn{জন্মাল}, \emph{sei shishu hāspātāle jônmālô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জন্মানো}} (\emph{jônmāno}) is the verb of \bn{জন্ম}, \textquotedblleft{}birth\textquotedblright{}, Sanskrit \emph{janman} (CDIAL 5113), the first half of \bn{জন্মদিন} (taught).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jônmāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jônmāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmār bhāijhi shīter ek sôkāle jônmālô.} — My niece was born one winter morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for pregnant, then the Bengali for childbirth, then say \emph{jônmāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাচ্চা} (bāchchā)}{বাচ্চা (bāchchā)}]{\bn{বাচ্চা} (bāchchā) — a baby; a small child}

\label{lesson:BN-C485-bachcha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for childbirth, then the Bengali for to be born.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাচ্চা}}
\textbf{\bn{বাচ্চা}} — \emph{bāchchā} — \textquotedblleft{}a baby; a small child\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাচ্চাটা} \bn{সারারাত} \bn{কাঁদল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāchchāṭā sārārāt kā̃dlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The baby cried all night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাচ্চা}} (\emph{bāchchā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bachcha}, \textquotedblleft{}a child, the young of an animal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দোলনা} (dolnā)}{দোলনা (dolnā)}]{\bn{দোলনা} (dolnā) — a cradle; a swing}

\label{lesson:BN-C485-dolna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to be born, then the Bengali for a baby.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দোলনা}}
\textbf{\bn{দোলনা}} — \emph{dolnā} — \textquotedblleft{}a cradle; a swing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাচ্চাটা} \bn{দোলনায়} \bn{শুয়ে} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāchchāṭā dolnāy shuye āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The baby is lying in the cradle.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দোলনা}} (\emph{dolnā}) is built on the verb \emph{dolā}, \textquotedblleft{}to swing\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists for Bengali under Sanskrit \emph{dōlāyate}, \textquotedblleft{}swings\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6585).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to be born, then the Bengali for a baby, then say \emph{dolnā} again
\end{itemize}
